newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian Commodities Roundup - Sept 17.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian Commodities Roundup - Sept 17.

text.p: World industrial metal prices took another turn for the worse on Monday, extending recent declines as bearish sentiment swamped the market.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau Index closed 1.67 points lower at 244.18.
Traders said consumer interest for all metals remained soft despite low prices, scotching hopes of a pick-up in demand during the traditionally busy September buying period.

Aluminium, used mainly in transport and packaging, slumped to a 2-1/2 year low of $1,414 a tonne on the London Metal Exchange (LME), down $22 from Friday's closing levels. Rising stocks and only sporadic buying interest left the market vulnerable to further losses, traders said.
Recent stock increases also weighed on the lead market, which slumped three percent, or $24 to $785.
Nickel fell to a 2-1/2 week low of $7,350 despite weekend production cutbacks at Inco's plant in Manitoba, Canada, while tin matched Friday's six-week nadir of $6,110.

Copper and zinc were less volatile, finishing the day with limited losses. In copper, the midsession pricing against the prime date was routine and signalled subsequent light selling and freer offers of metal on the nearby spreads. Cash/threes was around $6 backwardation at one stage before finishing at $9/10, still down from Friday's $18 premium.

Stocks are expected to be drawn down in the next few weeks, although Tuesday's LME data may not show these declines. Prices held close to the $1,860 level throughout the session, closing at $1,865, down just $5.

CBOT wheat futures closed lower and new contract lows were set in the March and May with news over the weekend that Egypt bought French rather than U.S. wheat, pulling values down, traders said. "Egypt buying wheat from France didn't help, that's bearish too..the increased global competition," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds. The new contract low for March is $4.09 per bushel, below the previous low of $4.20 set Friday. The new low for May is $3.95 per bushel, below the previous low of $4.04 also set Friday. Wheat closed one to 8-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with September dhicago soybeans broke below the key $8.00-a-bushel barrier, with November slipping 13 cents to $7.89. Wheat futures were seven cents lower at $4.22.
Oil was also weaker as tensions in the Middle East appeared to be easing.

The nearby futures contract for the benchmark North Sea Brent Blend on the International Petroleum Exchange in London was trading below $22.40 per barrel compared with a post-Gulf War high at $24.39 on September 12.

CSCE world sugar futures settled near the day's lows on residual speculative liquidation and selling of the October/March spread, market sources said. The October/March spread narrowed to 0.16 compared to 0.19 at Friday's close while the October contract, down for the fourth consecutive day, managed to hold above key support seen at 11.50. Below 11.50, the contract could sink to between 11.25 and 11.00, market sources said. March also held Friday's low of 11.35, forming a double bottom on the charts.
